### Course Description {.unnumbered}

This course is a rigorous introduction to the mathematical structures and reasoning techniques underlying computer science.
Topics include sets, functions, relations, graphs, trees, and finite automata,
with an emphasis on formal definitions and logical precision.
You will learn to write mathematical proofs
using direct proof, contrapositive, contradiction, and induction.
Functional programming is introduced as a way to express computation and recursion
within a mathematically grounded framework.

### Course Outcomes {.unnumbered}

Homework, labs, and exams test and measure the outcomes below.
On completion of CSCI 201, students will demonstrate:

- A thorough understanding of the mathematical definitions of concepts important to computer science,
  including sets, tuples, functions, and relations.
- A basic understanding of graphs, trees, and their traversals.
- A basic understanding of the mathematical definition of finite automata.
- A basic understanding of asymptotic notation.
- A basic understanding of recurrence relations and loop invariants.
- The ability to prove basic theorems involving these concepts
  using direct proof, contradiction, contrapositive, and mathematical induction.
- The ability to use functional style effectively in a functional programming language.
